summary: A solid Cortex/Mimir-like hot+cold metrics architecture with strong multi-tenant isolation, strict cardinality controls, and object-store-backed TSDB blocks for long retention. The design is broadly production-ready and covers key failure modes, but some simplifications (single query engine doing frontend+store duties, gossip-only ring) need careful hardening at large scale.
strengths: Strong multi-tenant isolation primitives (shuffle sharding, per-tenant budgets, reject-new-series under pressure) aligned with high-cardinality realities
Clear durability and storage story (quorum ack + WAL fsync, immutable blocks, compaction/retention/deletes) with practical degraded-mode behavior when object storage is unhealthy
weaknesses: Risky consolidation points: query engine replacing query-frontend/store-gateway and Postgres as a unified control plane can become bottlenecks without explicit HA, caching, and load-shedding details

Ring/replication operational details are underspecified (membership correctness, token persistence edge cases, rebalancing, replay/recovery time, and cross-AZ/network partitions) which can dominate real-world incident behavior at stated scale
